After a substantial amount of work, I'm finally ready to launch the first public version of my new mod, Trails of Tooth and Claw

At its core this is an exploration mod, so I won't be giving you a detailed rundown of all the content this mod adds. But enough time has passed since release, so for those not adverse to spoilers.

Spoiler
This mod adds three sub-factions collectively representing the Arkaran, a species of sapient bipedal reptiles, the campaign.

They have come from very far away, arriving at the sector's western border several months after the start of a campaign. Their purpose here is primarily to trade, but they are not planning to stay. During the campaign they will settle various star systems temporarily as they gradually make their way eastward across the campaign map in what I would describe as a rolling ecosystem separate from the core worlds. Eventually, once they reach the eastern border of the map, they will leave, permanently.

For now, detailed and nuanced interactions for affecting their trip through the sector are scant, and adding unique dialogue is a never-ending work in progress. But how you choose to react, or not react to their presence is entirely up to you.

This was a long time in the making, and involved many, many people in some capacity. It's still got some rough edges to polish up, and we hope to continue updating the project going forward. But for now, I hope everyone enjoys this 1.0 Release!

Also because I know people are going to ask:
- Yes, this mod functionally replaces LoA for me, the ideas I was building toward in LoA are more refined and better executed here in ways that appeal to my modern sensibilities far better than any of my long term plans for that mod ever could. I just don't have the interest in putting in the titanic amount of work it would require to continue developing content for that mod.

- No, I will not deprecate LoA, I will continue to ensure the mod continues to function through subsequent updates to the game, I just won't be developing any new content for it.

- Yes, you're allowed to be disappointed by that.

- No, it won't change my mind.
